Therefore t=w^2 satisfies t_(n+1)=t_n+4+4/t_n. The lower bound t_0+4n and summation give t_n=4n+O(log n); 4/t_k-1/k=O(log(k+1)/k^2) is absolutely summable and yields the finite orbit-dependent centered residual, with coefficient +1 on log n. Sign alternation gives opposite parity escapes, and increasing t excludes cycles. Escape from every compact and invariance applied to its indicator, followed by compact exhaustion of the punctured line, exclude invariant Borel probabilities.
